framework.name: ROBUST Framework
framework.preferred_phrase: The Watchdog Score is powered by the ROBUST Framework.
framework.explanation_phrase: Watchdog tells you where you stand. ROBUST tells you why.

dimensions.name: Overassessment Position
dimensions.compatibility_note: The current score implementation retains the internal key fairness. Public presentation must use O - Overassessment Position.

dimensions.name: Uniformity
dimensions.legacy_surface_note: COD-driven surfaces historically labeled Assessment Fairness belong conceptually under U - Uniformity.

dimensions.name: Stability
dimensions.micro_definition: Pressure for reassessment or structural change.

dimensions.name: Trajectory
dimensions.micro_definition: Direction of the property's tax position.

rules: Do not rename the Watchdog Score to ROBUST Score.
Always write O as Overassessment Position, not merely Overassessment.
Do not use ROBUST as a desirability label for a home, person, neighborhood, municipality, county or government.
Do not change current weights or formulas as a branding-only change.
Keep experimental or fallback scores outside the unqualified Watchdog Score and ROBUST names unless they pass the canonical score contract.
Keep protected-class and demographic characteristics out of the core score.
When a COD-driven surface is touched, use U - Uniformity language instead of naming COD itself Assessment Fairness.
Public score explanations should expose the six dimensions in R-O-B-U-S-T order when practical.
